`attach` was resolving Codex sessions as flat files under `~/.codex/<session-id>.jsonl`, but your actual session exists in the dated sessions tree:
`~/.codex/sessions/2026/04/08/rollout-2026-04-08T10-43-48-019d6c43-1537-7343-9691-1f8cee04fe59.jsonl`.

- uses `CODEX_HOME/sessions` as the base directory
- finds `rollout-...-<session-id>.jsonl` in the `YYYY/MM/DD` tree
- still preserves absolute-path handling from hooks

I also added regression coverage in [codex_test.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/codex_test.go) and an end-to-end attach test in [attach_test.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/attach_test.go).

I double-checked. This probably did not start failing because Codex changed today.

What changed is:

- The Codex integration was added on March 25, 2026 in commit `eeaa9074b`.
- In that first version, `ResolveSessionFile()` explicitly said it could not resolve a transcript from only a session ID, so `attach` for Codex was effectively unsupported.
- Later that same day, commit `83b778e61` changed it to a “best-effort” flat path lookup, which assumed `~/.codex/<session-id>.jsonl`.
- Your actual Codex files have been in `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-...-<session-id>.jsonl`, and I can see local files in that layout going back to March 18, 2026.

So the issue is: Codex `attach` was never correctly implemented for session-ID-only lookup. It just became visible now because this is the path that exercises it.

Why normal Codex usage still worked:
- Hook-driven flows pass the absolute `transcript_path` from Codex, so they never relied on reconstructing the file from the session ID.
- `attach` is different: it starts with only the session ID, so the bad resolver mattered there.

I don’t see evidence that `codex-cli 0.118.0` introduced this. The storage layout on your machine predates the integration. This looks like an integration gap plus missing test coverage, not a new upstream break.
